Just then, the doorbell rang \u2014\u201cOh, good Lord, they\u2019re here!\u201d said Aunt Petunia frantically \u2014 and a moment later, Dudley\u2019s best friend, Piers Polkiss, walked in with his mother. Piers was a scrawny boy with a face like a rat. He was usually the one who held people\u2019s arms behind their backs while Dudley hit them. Dudley stopped pretending to cry at once. Half an hour later, Harry, who couldn\u2019t believe his luck, was sitting in the back of the Dursleys\u2019 car with Piers and Dudley, on the way to the zoo for the first time in his life. His aunt and uncle hadn\u2019t been able to think of anything else to do with him, but before they\u2019d left, Uncle Vernon had taken Harry aside. \u201cI\u2019m warning you,\u201d he had said, putting his large purple face right up close to Harry\u2019s, \u201cI\u2019m warning you now, boy \u2014 any funny business, anything at all \u2014 and you\u2019ll be in that cupboard from now until Christmas.\u201d

Three things lay on the doormat: a postcard from Uncle Vernon\u2019s sister Marge, who was vacationing on the Isle of Wight, a brown envelope that looked like a bill, and \u2014 a letter for Harry. Harry picked it up and stared at it, his heart twanging like a giant elastic band. No one, ever, in his whole life, had written to him. Who would? He had no friends, no other relatives \u2014 he didn\u2019t belong to the library, so he\u2019d never even got rude notes asking for books back. Yet here it was, a letter, addressed so plainly there could be no mistake: Mr. H. Potter The Cupboard under the Stairs 4 Privet Drive Little Whinging Surrey The envelope was thick and heavy, made of yellowish parchment, and the address was written in emerald-green ink. There was no stamp. The giant sat back down on the sofa, which sagged under his weight, and began taking all sorts of things out of the pockets of his coat: a copper kettle, a squashy package of sausages, a poker, a teapot, several chipped mugs, and a bottle of some amber liquid that he took a swig from before starting to make tea. Nobody said a thing while the giant was working, but as he slid the first six fat, juicy, slightly burnt sausages from the poker, Dudley fidgeted a little. I knew yeh weren\u2019t gettin\u2019 yer letters but I never thought yeh wouldn\u2019t even know abou\u2019 Hogwarts, fer cryin\u2019 out loud! Then he came back and sat down as though this was as normal as talking on the telephone. Harry realized his mouth was open and closed it quickly. \u201cWhere was I?\u201d said Hagrid, but at that moment, Uncle Vernon, still ashen-faced but looking very angry, moved into the firelight. \u201cHe\u2019s not going,\u201d he said. Hagrid grunted. \u201cI\u2019d like ter see a great Muggle like you stop him,\u201d he said. \u201cA what?\u201d said Harry, interested. \u201cA Muggle,\u201d said Hagrid, \u201cit\u2019s what we call nonmagic folk like them. An\u2019 it\u2019s your bad luck you grew up in a family o\u2019 the biggest Muggles I ever laid eyes on.\u201d \u201cWe swore when we took him in we\u2019d put a stop to that rubbish,\u201d said Uncle Vernon, \u201cswore we\u2019d stamp it out of him! Wizard indeed!\u201d \u201cYou knew?\u201d said Harry. \u201cYou knew I\u2019m a \u2014 a wizard?\u201d \u201cKnew!\u201d shrieked Aunt Petunia suddenly. \u201cKnew! Of course we knew! How could you not be, my dratted sister being what she was? Oh, she got a letter just like that and disappeared off to that \u2014 that school \u2014 and came home every vacation with her pockets full of frog spawn, turning teacups into rats. I was the only one who saw her for what she was \u2014 a freak! But for my mother and father, oh no, it was Lily this and Lily that, they were proud of having a witch in the family!\u201d She stopped to draw a deep breath and then went ranting on. It seemed she had been wanting to say all this for years. \u201cThen she met that Potter at school and they left and got married and had you, and of course I knew you\u2019d be just the same, just as strange, just as \u2014 as \u2014 abnormal \u2014 and then, if you please, she went and got herself blown up and we got landed with you!\u201d Harry had gone very white. As soon as he found his voice he said, \u201cBlown up? You told me they died in a car crash!\u201d \u201cCAR CRASH!\u201d roared Hagrid, jumping up so angrily that the Dursleys scuttled back to their corner. \u201cHow could a car crash kill Lily an\u2019 James Potter? It\u2019s an outrage! A scandal! Harry Potter not knowin\u2019 his own story when every kid in our world knows his name!\u201d \u201cBut why? What happened?\u201d Harry asked urgently. The anger faded from Hagrid\u2019s face. He looked suddenly anxious. \u201cI never expected this,\u201d he said, in a low, worried voice. \u201cI had no idea, when Dumbledore told me there might be trouble gettin\u2019 hold of yeh, how much yeh didn\u2019t know. Ah, Harry, I don\u2019 know if I\u2019m the right person ter tell yeh \u2014 but someone\u2019s gotta \u2014 yeh can\u2019t go off ter Hogwarts not knowin\u2019.\u201d He threw a dirty look at the Dursleys. \u201cWell, it\u2019s best yeh know as much as I can tell yeh \u2014 mind, I can\u2019t tell yeh everythin\u2019, it\u2019s a great myst\u2019ry, parts of it. . . .\u201d He sat down, stared into the fire for a few seconds, and then said, \u201cIt begins, I suppose, with \u2014 with a person called \u2014 but it\u2019s incredible yeh don\u2019t know his name, everyone in our world knows \u2014\u201d \u201cWho?\u201d \u201cWell \u2014 I don\u2019 like sayin\u2019 the name if I can help it. No one does.\u201d \u201cWhy not?\u201d \u201cGulpin\u2019 gargoyles, Harry, people are still scared. Blimey, this is difficult. See, there was this wizard who went . . . bad. As bad as you could go. Worse. Worse than worse. His name was . . .\u201d Hagrid gulped, but no words came out. \u201cCould you write it down?\u201d Harry suggested. \u201cNah \u2014 can\u2019t spell it. All right \u2014 Voldemort.\u201d Hagrid shuddered. \u201cDon\u2019 make me say it again. Anyway, this \u2014 this wizard, about twenty years ago now, started lookin\u2019 fer followers. Got \u2019em, too \u2014 some were afraid, some just wanted a bit o\u2019 his power, \u2019cause he was gettin\u2019 himself power, all right. Dark days, Harry. Didn\u2019t know who ter trust, didn\u2019t dare get friendly with strange wizards or witches . . . terrible things happened. He was takin\u2019 over. \u2019Course, some stood up to him \u2014 an\u2019 he killed \u2019em. Horribly. One o\u2019 the only safe places left was Hogwarts. Reckon Dumbledore\u2019s the only one You-Know-Who was afraid of. Didn\u2019t dare try takin\u2019 the school, not jus\u2019 then, anyway. \u201cNow, yer mum an\u2019 dad were as good a witch an\u2019 wizard as I ever knew. Head boy an\u2019 girl at Hogwarts in their day! Suppose the myst\u2019ry is why You-Know-Who never tried to get \u2019em on his side before . . . probably knew they were too close ter Dumbledore ter want anythin\u2019 ter do with the Dark Side. \u201cMaybe he thought he could persuade \u2019em . . . maybe he just wanted \u2019em outta the way. All anyone knows is, he turned up in the village where you was all living, on Halloween ten years ago. You was just a year old. He came ter yer house an\u2019\u2014 an\u2019\u2014 \u201d Hagrid suddenly pulled out a very dirty, spotted handkerchief and blew his nose with a sound like a foghorn. \u201cSorry,\u201d he said. \u201cBut it\u2019s that sad \u2014 knew yer mum an\u2019 dad, an\u2019 nicer people yeh couldn\u2019t find \u2014 anyway . . . \u201cYou-Know-Who killed \u2019em. An\u2019 then \u2014 an\u2019 this is the real myst\u2019ry of the thing \u2014 he tried to kill you, too. Wanted ter make a clean job of it, I suppose, or maybe he just liked killin\u2019 by then. But he couldn\u2019t do it. Never wondered how you got that mark on yer forehead? That was no ordinary cut. That\u2019s what yeh get when a powerful, evil curse touches yeh \u2014 took care of yer mum an\u2019 dad an\u2019 yer house, even \u2014 but it didn\u2019t work on you, an\u2019 that\u2019s why yer famous, Harry. No one ever lived after he decided ter kill \u2019em, no one except you, an\u2019 he\u2019d killed some o\u2019 the best witches an\u2019 wizards of the age \u2014 the McKinnons, the Bones, the Prewetts \u2014 an\u2019 you was only a baby, an\u2019 you lived.\u201d Something very painful was going on in Harry\u2019s mind. As Hagrid\u2019s story came to a close, he saw again the blinding flash of green light, more clearly than he had ever remembered it before \u2014 and he remembered something else, for the first time in his life: a high, cold, cruel laugh. Hagrid was watching him sadly. \u201cTook yeh from the ruined house myself, on Dumbledore\u2019s orders. Brought yeh ter this lot . . .\u201d \u201cLoad of old tosh,\u201d said Uncle Vernon. Harry jumped; he had almost forgotten that the Dursleys were there. Uncle Vernon certainly seemed to have got back his courage. He was glaring at Hagrid and his fists were clenched. \u201cNow, you listen here, boy,\u201d he snarled, \u201cI accept there\u2019s something strange about you, probably nothing a good beating wouldn\u2019t have cured \u2014 and as for all this about your parents, well, they were weirdos, no denying it, and the world\u2019s better off without them in my opinion \u2014 asked for all they got, getting mixed up with these wizarding types \u2014 just what I expected, always knew they\u2019d come to a sticky end \u2014\u201d But at that moment, Hagrid leapt from the sofa and drew a battered pink umbrella from inside his coat. Pointing this at Uncle Vernon like a sword, he said, \u201cI\u2019m warning you, Dursley \u2014 I\u2019m warning you \u2014 one more word . . .\u201d In danger of being speared on the end of an umbrella by a bearded giant, Uncle Vernon\u2019s courage failed again; he flattened himself against the wall and fell silent. \u201cThat\u2019s better,\u201d said Hagrid, breathing heavily and sitting back down on the sofa, which this time sagged right down to the floor. Harry, meanwhile, still had questions to ask, hundreds of them. \u201cBut what happened to Vol-, sorry \u2014 I mean, You-Know-Who?\u201d \u201cGood question, Harry. Disappeared. Vanished. Same night he tried ter kill you. Makes yeh even more famous. That\u2019s the biggest myst\u2019ry, see . . . he was gettin\u2019 more an\u2019 more powerful \u2014 why\u2019d he go? \u201cSome say he died. Codswallop, in my opinion. Dunno if he had enough human left in him to die. Some say he\u2019s still out there, bidin\u2019 his time, like, but I don\u2019 believe it. People who was on his side came back ter ours. Some of \u2019em came outta kinda trances. Don\u2019 reckon they could\u2019ve done if he was comin\u2019 back. \u201cMost of us reckon he\u2019s still out there somewhere but lost his powers. Too weak to carry on. \u2019Cause somethin\u2019 about you finished him, Harry. There was somethin\u2019 goin\u2019 on that night he hadn\u2019t counted on \u2014 I dunno what it was, no one does \u2014 but somethin\u2019 about you stumped him, all right.\u201d Hagrid looked at Harry with warmth and respect blazing in his eyes, but Harry, instead of feeling pleased and proud, felt quite sure there had been a horrible mistake. A wizard? Him? How could he possibly be? He\u2019d spent his life being clouted by Dudley, and bullied by Aunt Petunia and Uncle Vernon; if he was really a wizard, why hadn\u2019t they been turned into warty toads every time they\u2019d tried to lock him in his cupboard? If he\u2019d once defeated the greatest sorcerer in the world, how come Dudley had always been able to kick him around like a football? \u201cHagrid,\u201d he said quietly, \u201cI think you must have made a mistake. I don\u2019t think I can be a wizard.\u201d To his surprise, Hagrid chuckled. \u201cNot a wizard, eh? Never made things happen when you was scared or angry?\u201d Harry looked into the fire. Now he came to think about it . . . every odd thing that had ever made his aunt and uncle furious with him had happened when he, Harry, had been upset or angry . . . chased by Dudley\u2019s gang, he had somehow found himself out of their reach . . . dreading going to school with that ridiculous haircut, he\u2019d managed to make it grow back . . . and the very last time Dudley had hit him, hadn\u2019t he got his revenge, without even realizing he was doing it? Hadn\u2019t he set a boa constrictor on him? Harry looked back at Hagrid, smiling, and saw that Hagrid was positively beaming at him. \u201cSee?\u201d said Hagrid. \u201cHarry Potter, not a wizard \u2014 you wait, you\u2019ll be right famous at Hogwarts.\u201d But Uncle Vernon wasn\u2019t going to give in without a fight. \u201cHaven\u2019t I told you he\u2019s not going?\u201d he hissed. \u201cHe\u2019s going to Stonewall High and he\u2019ll be grateful for it. I\u2019ve read those letters and he needs all sorts of rubbish \u2014 spell books and wands and \u2014\u201d \u201cIf he wants ter go, a great Muggle like you won\u2019t stop him,\u201d growled Hagrid. \u201cStop Lily an\u2019 James Potter\u2019s son goin\u2019 ter Hogwarts! Yer mad. His name\u2019s been down ever since he was born. He\u2019s off ter the finest school of witchcraft and wizardry in the world. Seven years there and he won\u2019t know himself. He\u2019ll be with youngsters of his own sort, fer a change, an\u2019 he\u2019ll be under the greatest headmaster Hogwarts ever had, Albus Dumbled \u2014\u201d \u201cI AM NOT PAYING FOR SOME CRACKPOT OLD FOOL TO TEACH HIM MAGIC TRICKS!\u201d yelled Uncle Vernon. But he had finally gone too far. Hagrid seized his umbrella and whirled it over his head, \u201cNEVER \u2014\u201d he thundered, \u201c\u2014 INSULT \u2014 ALBUS \u2014 DUMBLEDORE \u2014 IN \u2014 FRONT \u2014 OF \u2014 ME!\u201d He brought the umbrella swishing down through the air to point at Dudley \u2014 there was a flash of violet light, a sound like a firecracker, a sharp squeal, and the next second, Dudley was dancing on the spot with his hands clasped over his fat bottom, howling in pain. When he turned his back on them, Harry saw a curly pig\u2019s tail poking through a hole in his trousers. Uncle Vernon roared. Pulling Aunt Petunia and Dudley into the other room, he cast one last terrified look at Hagrid and slammed the door behind them. Hagrid looked down at his umbrella and stroked his beard. \u201cShouldn\u2019ta lost me temper,\u201d he said ruefully, \u201cbut it didn\u2019t work anyway. Meant ter turn him into a pig, but I suppose he was so much like a pig anyway there wasn\u2019t much left ter do.\u201d He cast a sideways look at Harry under his bushy eyebrows. \u201cBe grateful if yeh didn\u2019t mention that ter anyone at Hogwarts,\u201d he said. \u201cI\u2019m \u2014 er \u2014 not supposed ter do magic, strictly speakin\u2019. I was allowed ter do a bit ter follow yeh an\u2019 get yer letters to yeh an\u2019 stuff \u2014 one o\u2019 the reasons I was so keen ter take on the job \u2014\u201d \u201cWhy aren\u2019t you supposed to do magic?\u201d asked Harry. \u201cOh, well \u2014 I was at Hogwarts meself but I \u2014 er \u2014 got expelled, ter tell yeh the truth. In me third year. They snapped me wand in half an\u2019 everything. But Dumbledore let me stay on as gamekeeper. Great man, Dumbledore.\u201d \u201cWhy were you expelled?\u201d \u201cIt\u2019s gettin\u2019 late and we\u2019ve got lots ter do tomorrow,\u201d said Hagrid loudly. \u201cGotta get up ter town, get all yer books an\u2019 that.\u201d He took off his thick black coat and threw it to Harry. \u201cYou can kip under that,\u201d he said. \u201cDon\u2019 mind if it wriggles a bit, I think I still got a couple o\u2019 dormice in one o\u2019 the pockets.\u201d

Worse. Worse than worse. His name was . . .\u201d Hagrid gulped, but no words came out. \u201cCould you write it down?\u201d Harry suggested. \u201cNah \u2014 can\u2019t spell it. All right \u2014 Voldemort.\u201d Hagrid shuddered. \u201cDon\u2019 make me say it again. Anyway, this \u2014 this wizard, about twenty years ago now, started lookin\u2019 fer followers. Got \u2019em, too \u2014 some were afraid, some just wanted a bit o\u2019 his power, \u2019cause he was gettin\u2019 himself power, all right. Dark days, Harry. Didn\u2019t know who ter trust, didn\u2019t dare get friendly with strange wizards or witches . . . terrible things happened. He was takin\u2019 over. \u2019Course, some stood up to him \u2014 an\u2019 he killed \u2019em. Horribly. One o\u2019 the only safe places left was Hogwarts. Reckon Dumbledore\u2019s the only one You-Know-Who was afraid of. Didn\u2019t dare try takin\u2019 the school, not jus\u2019 then, anyway. \u201cNow, yer mum an\u2019 dad were as good a witch an\u2019 wizard as I ever knew. Head boy an\u2019 girl at Hogwarts in their day! Suppose the myst\u2019ry is why You-Know-Who never tried to get \u2019em on his side before . . . probably knew they were too close ter Dumbledore ter want anythin\u2019 ter do with the Dark Side. \u201cMaybe he thought he could persuade \u2019em . . . maybe he just wanted \u2019em outta the way. All anyone knows is, he turned up in the village where you was all living, on Halloween ten years ago. You was just a year old. He came ter yer house an\u2019\u2014 an\u2019\u2014 \u201d Hagrid suddenly pulled out a very dirty, spotted handkerchief and blew his nose with a sound like a foghorn. \u201cSorry,\u201d he said. \u201cBut it\u2019s that sad \u2014 knew yer mum an\u2019 dad, an\u2019 nicer people yeh couldn\u2019t find \u2014 anyway . . . \u201cYou-Know-Who killed \u2019em. An\u2019 then \u2014 an\u2019 this is the real myst\u2019ry of the thing \u2014 he tried to kill you, too. Wanted ter make a clean job of it, I suppose, or maybe he just liked killin\u2019 by then. But he couldn\u2019t do it. Never wondered how you got that mark on yer forehead? That was no ordinary cut. That\u2019s what yeh get when a powerful, evil curse touches yeh \u2014 took care of yer mum an\u2019 dad an\u2019 yer house, even \u2014 but it didn\u2019t work on you, an\u2019 that\u2019s why yer famous, Harry. No one ever lived after he decided ter kill \u2019em, no one except you, an\u2019 he\u2019d killed some o\u2019 the best witches an\u2019 wizards of the age \u2014 the McKinnons, the Bones, the Prewetts \u2014 an\u2019 you was only a baby, an\u2019 you lived.\u201d Something very painful was going on in Harry\u2019s mind. As Hagrid\u2019s story came to a close, he saw again the blinding flash of green light, more clearly than he had ever remembered it before \u2014 and he remembered something else, for the first time in his life: a high, cold, cruel laugh. Hagrid was watching him sadly. \u201cTook yeh from the ruined house myself, on Dumbledore\u2019s orders. Brought yeh ter this lot . . .\u201d \u201cLoad of old tosh,\u201d said Uncle Vernon. Harry jumped; he had almost forgotten that the Dursleys were there. Uncle Vernon certainly seemed to have got back his courage. He was glaring at Hagrid and his fists were clenched. \u201cNow, you listen here, boy,\u201d he snarled, \u201cI accept there\u2019s something strange about you, probably nothing a good beating wouldn\u2019t have cured \u2014 and as for all this about your parents, well, they were weirdos, no denying it, and the world\u2019s better off without them in my opinion \u2014 asked for all they got, getting mixed up with these wizarding types \u2014 just what I expected, always knew they\u2019d come to a sticky end \u2014\u201d But at that moment, Hagrid leapt from the sofa and drew a battered pink umbrella from inside his coat. Pointing this at Uncle Vernon like a sword, he said, \u201cI\u2019m warning you, Dursley \u2014 I\u2019m warning you \u2014 one more word . . .\u201d In danger of being speared on the end of an umbrella by a bearded giant, Uncle Vernon\u2019s courage failed again; he flattened himself against the wall and fell silent. \u201cThat\u2019s better,\u201d said Hagrid, breathing heavily and sitting back down on the sofa, which this time sagged right down to the floor. Harry, meanwhile, still had questions to ask, hundreds of them. \u201cBut what happened to Vol-, sorry \u2014 I mean, You-Know-Who?\u201d \u201cGood question, Harry. Disappeared. Vanished. Same night he tried ter kill you. Makes yeh even more famous. That\u2019s the biggest myst\u2019ry, see . . . he was gettin\u2019 more an\u2019 more powerful \u2014 why\u2019d he go? \u201cSome say he died. Codswallop, in my opinion. Dunno if he had enough human left in him to die. Some say he\u2019s still out there, bidin\u2019 his time, like, but I don\u2019 believe it. People who was on his side came back ter ours. Some of \u2019em came outta kinda trances. Don\u2019 reckon they could\u2019ve done if he was comin\u2019 back. \u201cMost of us reckon he\u2019s still out there somewhere but lost his powers. Too weak to carry on. \u2019Cause somethin\u2019 about you finished him, Harry. There was somethin\u2019 goin\u2019 on that night he hadn\u2019t counted on \u2014 I dunno what it was, no one does \u2014 but somethin\u2019 about you stumped him, all right.\u201d Hagrid looked at Harry with warmth and respect blazing in his eyes, but Harry, instead of feeling pleased and proud, felt quite sure there had been a horrible mistake. A wizard? Him? How could he possibly be? He\u2019d spent his life being clouted by Dudley, and bullied by Aunt Petunia and Uncle Vernon; if he was really a wizard, why hadn\u2019t they been turned into warty toads every time they\u2019d tried to lock him in his cupboard? If he\u2019d once defeated the greatest sorcerer in the world, how come Dudley had always been able to kick him around like a football? \u201cHagrid,\u201d he said quietly, \u201cI think you must have made a mistake. I don\u2019t think I can be a wizard.\u201d To his surprise, Hagrid chuckled. \u201cNot a wizard, eh? Never made things happen when you was scared or angry?\u201d Harry looked into the fire. Now he came to think about it . . . every odd thing that had ever made his aunt and uncle furious with him had happened when he, Harry, had been upset or angry . . . chased by Dudley\u2019s gang, he had somehow found himself out of their reach . . . dreading going to school with that ridiculous haircut, he\u2019d managed to make it grow back . . . and the very last time Dudley had hit him, hadn\u2019t he got his revenge, without even realizing he was doing it? Hadn\u2019t he set a boa constrictor on him? Harry looked back at Hagrid, smiling, and saw that Hagrid was positively beaming at him. \u201cSee?\u201d said Hagrid. \u201cHarry Potter, not a wizard \u2014 you wait, you\u2019ll be right famous at Hogwarts.\u201d But Uncle Vernon wasn\u2019t going to give in without a fight. \u201cHaven\u2019t I told you he\u2019s not going?\u201d he hissed. \u201cHe\u2019s going to Stonewall High and he\u2019ll be grateful for it. I\u2019ve read those letters and he needs all sorts of rubbish \u2014 spell books and wands and \u2014\u201d \u201cIf he wants ter go, a great Muggle like you won\u2019t stop him,\u201d growled Hagrid. \u201cStop Lily an\u2019 James Potter\u2019s son goin\u2019 ter Hogwarts! Yer mad. His name\u2019s been down ever since he was born. He\u2019s off ter the finest school of witchcraft and wizardry in the world. Seven years there and he won\u2019t know himself. He\u2019ll be with youngsters of his own sort, fer a change, an\u2019 he\u2019ll be under the greatest headmaster Hogwarts ever had, Albus Dumbled \u2014\u201d \u201cI AM NOT PAYING FOR SOME CRACKPOT OLD FOOL TO TEACH HIM MAGIC TRICKS!\u201d yelled Uncle Vernon. But he had finally gone too far. Hagrid seized his umbrella and whirled it over his head, \u201cNEVER \u2014\u201d he thundered, \u201c\u2014 INSULT \u2014 ALBUS \u2014 DUMBLEDORE \u2014 IN \u2014 FRONT \u2014 OF \u2014 ME!\u201d He brought the umbrella swishing down through the air to point at Dudley \u2014 there was a flash of violet light, a sound like a firecracker, a sharp squeal, and the next second, Dudley was dancing on the spot with his hands clasped over his fat bottom, howling in pain. When he turned his back on them, Harry saw a curly pig\u2019s tail poking through a hole in his trousers. Uncle Vernon roared. Pulling Aunt Petunia and Dudley into the other room, he cast one last terrified look at Hagrid and slammed the door behind them. Hagrid looked down at his umbrella and stroked his beard. \u201cShouldn\u2019ta lost me temper,\u201d he said ruefully, \u201cbut it didn\u2019t work anyway. Meant ter turn him into a pig, but I suppose he was so much like a pig anyway there wasn\u2019t much left ter do.\u201d He cast a sideways look at Harry under his bushy eyebrows. \u201cBe grateful if yeh didn\u2019t mention that ter anyone at Hogwarts,\u201d he said. \u201cI\u2019m \u2014 er \u2014 not supposed ter do magic, strictly speakin\u2019. I was allowed ter do a bit ter follow yeh an\u2019 get yer letters to yeh an\u2019 stuff \u2014 one o\u2019 the reasons I was so keen ter take on the job \u2014\u201d \u201cWhy aren\u2019t you supposed to do magic?\u201d asked Harry. \u201cOh, well \u2014 I was at Hogwarts meself but I \u2014 er \u2014 got expelled, ter tell yeh the truth. In me third year. They snapped me wand in half an\u2019 everything. But Dumbledore let me stay on as gamekeeper. Great man, Dumbledore.\u201d \u201cWhy were you expelled?\u201d \u201cIt\u2019s gettin\u2019 late and we\u2019ve got lots ter do tomorrow,\u201d said Hagrid loudly. \u201cGotta get up ter town, get all yer books an\u2019 that.\u201d He took off his thick black coat and threw it to Harry. \u201cYou can kip under that,\u201d he said. \u201cDon\u2019 mind if it wriggles a bit, I think I still got a couple o\u2019 dormice in one o\u2019 the pockets.\u201d

That\u2019s what yeh get when a powerful, evil curse touches yeh \u2014 took care of yer mum an\u2019 dad an\u2019 yer house, even \u2014 but it didn\u2019t work on you, an\u2019 that\u2019s why yer famous, Harry. No one ever lived after he decided ter kill \u2019em, no one except you, an\u2019 he\u2019d killed some o\u2019 the best witches an\u2019 wizards of the age \u2014 the McKinnons, the Bones, the Prewetts \u2014 an\u2019 you was only a baby, an\u2019 you lived.\u201d Something very painful was going on in Harry\u2019s mind. Hagrid was watching him sadly. \u201cTook yeh from the ruined house myself, on Dumbledore\u2019s orders. Brought yeh ter this lot . . .\u201d \u201cLoad of old tosh,\u201d said Uncle Vernon. Harry jumped; he had almost forgotten that the Dursleys were there. Uncle Vernon certainly seemed to have got back his courage. He was glaring at Hagrid and his fists were clenched. \u201cNow, you listen here, boy,\u201d he snarled, \u201cI accept there\u2019s something strange about you, probably nothing a good beating wouldn\u2019t have cured \u2014 and as for all this about your parents, well, they were weirdos, no denying it, and the world\u2019s better off without them in my opinion \u2014 asked for all they got, getting mixed up with these wizarding types \u2014 just what I expected, always knew they\u2019d come to a sticky end \u2014\u201d But at that moment, Hagrid leapt from the sofa and drew a battered pink umbrella from inside his coat. Pointing this at Uncle Vernon like a sword, he said, \u201cI\u2019m warning you, Dursley \u2014 I\u2019m warning you \u2014 one more word . . .\u201d In danger of being speared on the end of an umbrella by a bearded giant, Uncle Vernon\u2019s courage failed again; he flattened himself against the wall and fell silent. \u201cThat\u2019s better,\u201d said Hagrid, breathing heavily and sitting back down on the sofa, which this time sagged right down to the floor. Harry, meanwhile, still had questions to ask, hundreds of them. \u201cBut what happened to Vol-, sorry \u2014 I mean, You-Know-Who?\u201d \u201cGood question, Harry. Disappeared. Vanished. Same night he tried ter kill you. Makes yeh even more famous. That\u2019s the biggest myst\u2019ry, see . . . he was gettin\u2019 more an\u2019 more powerful \u2014 why\u2019d he go? \u201cSome say he died. Codswallop, in my opinion. Dunno if he had enough human left in him to die. Some say he\u2019s still out there, bidin\u2019 his time, like, but I don\u2019 believe it. People who was on his side came back ter ours. Some of \u2019em came outta kinda trances. Don\u2019 reckon they could\u2019ve done if he was comin\u2019 back. \u201cMost of us reckon he\u2019s still out there somewhere but lost his powers. Too weak to carry on. \u2019Cause somethin\u2019 about you finished him, Harry. He\u2019d spent his life being clouted by Dudley, and bullied by Aunt Petunia and Uncle Vernon; if he was really a wizard, why hadn\u2019t they been turned into warty toads every time they\u2019d tried to lock him in his cupboard? If he\u2019d once defeated the greatest sorcerer in the world, how come Dudley had always been able to kick him around like a football? \u201cHagrid,\u201d he said quietly, \u201cI think you must have made a mistake. Hadn\u2019t he set a boa constrictor on him? Harry looked back at Hagrid, smiling, and saw that Hagrid was positively beaming at him. \u201cSee?\u201d said Hagrid. \u201cHarry Potter, not a wizard \u2014 you wait, you\u2019ll be right famous at Hogwarts.\u201d But Uncle Vernon wasn\u2019t going to give in without a fight. \u201cHaven\u2019t I told you he\u2019s not going?\u201d he hissed. \u201cHe\u2019s going to Stonewall High and he\u2019ll be grateful for it. I\u2019ve read those letters and he needs all sorts of rubbish \u2014 spell books and wands and \u2014\u201d \u201cIf he wants ter go, a great Muggle like you won\u2019t stop him,\u201d growled Hagrid. \u201cStop Lily an\u2019 James Potter\u2019s son goin\u2019 ter Hogwarts! Yer mad. His name\u2019s been down ever since he was born. He\u2019s off ter the finest school of witchcraft and wizardry in the world. Seven years there and he won\u2019t know himself. He\u2019ll be with youngsters of his own sort, fer a change, an\u2019 he\u2019ll be under the greatest headmaster Hogwarts ever had, Albus Dumbled \u2014\u201d \u201cI AM NOT PAYING FOR SOME CRACKPOT OLD FOOL TO TEACH HIM MAGIC TRICKS!\u201d yelled Uncle Vernon. Hagrid seized his umbrella and whirled it over his head, \u201cNEVER \u2014\u201d he thundered, \u201c\u2014 INSULT \u2014 ALBUS \u2014 DUMBLEDORE \u2014 IN \u2014 FRONT \u2014 OF \u2014 ME!\u201d He brought the umbrella swishing down through the air to point at Dudley \u2014 there was a flash of violet light, a sound like a firecracker, a sharp squeal, and the next second, Dudley was dancing on the spot with his hands clasped over his fat bottom, howling in pain. I was allowed ter do a bit ter follow yeh an\u2019 get yer letters to yeh an\u2019 stuff \u2014 one o\u2019 the reasons I was so keen ter take on the job \u2014\u201d \u201cWhy aren\u2019t you supposed to do magic?\u201d asked Harry. \u201cOh, well \u2014 I was at Hogwarts meself but I \u2014 er \u2014 got expelled, ter tell yeh the truth. In me third year. They snapped me wand in half an\u2019 everything. But Dumbledore let me stay on as gamekeeper. Great man, Dumbledore.\u201d \u201cWhy were you expelled?\u201d \u201cIt\u2019s gettin\u2019 late and we\u2019ve got lots ter do tomorrow,\u201d said Hagrid loudly. \u201cGotta get up ter town, get all yer books an\u2019 that.\u201d He took off his thick black coat and threw it to Harry. \u201cYou can kip under that,\u201d he said. \u201cDon\u2019 mind if it wriggles a bit, I think I still got a couple o\u2019 dormice in one o\u2019 the pockets.\u201d

gold_response: Oh, that was mental. I mean, I never had any idea I was a wizard or anything. Uncle Vernon and Aunt Petunia, they never told me anything about my parents being magical. So when this giant of a man, Hagrid, comes bursting through the door of that little hut on the rock in the sea, it was the biggest shock of my life. But he still didn\u2019t open his eyes. It had been such a good dream. Tap. Tap. Tap. \u201cAll right,\u201d Harry mumbled, \u201cI\u2019m getting up.\u201d He sat up and Hagrid\u2019s heavy coat fell off him. The hut was full of sunlight, the storm was over, Hagrid himself was asleep on the collapsed sofa, and there was an owl rapping its claw on the window, a newspaper held in its beak. Harry scrambled to his feet, so happy he felt as though a large balloon was swelling inside him. He went straight to the window and jerked it open. The owl swooped in and dropped the newspaper on top of Hagrid, who didn\u2019t wake up. The owl then fluttered onto the floor and began to attack Hagrid\u2019s coat. \u201cDon\u2019t do that.\u201d Harry tried to wave the owl out of the way, but it snapped its beak fiercely at him and carried on savaging the coat. \u201cHagrid!\u201d said Harry loudly. \u201cThere\u2019s an owl \u2014\u201d \u201cPay him,\u201d Hagrid grunted into the sofa. \u201cWhat?\u201d \u201cHe wants payin\u2019 fer deliverin\u2019 the paper. Then he flew off through the open window. Hagrid yawned loudly, sat up, and stretched. \u201cBest be off, Harry, lots ter do today, gotta get up ter London an\u2019 buy all yer stuff fer school.\u201d Harry was turning over the wizard coins and looking at them. He had just thought of something that made him feel as though the happy balloon inside him had got a puncture. \u201cUm \u2014 Hagrid?\u201d \u201cMm?\u201d said Hagrid, who was pulling on his huge boots. \u201cI haven\u2019t got any money \u2014 and you heard Uncle Vernon last night . . . he won\u2019t pay for me to go and learn magic.\u201d \u201cDon\u2019t worry about that,\u201d said Hagrid, standing up and scratching his head. \u201cD\u2019yeh think yer parents didn\u2019t leave yeh anything?\u201d \u201cBut if their house was destroyed \u2014\u201d \u201cThey didn\u2019 keep their gold in the house, boy! Nah, first stop fer us is Gringotts. Wizards\u2019 bank. Have a sausage, they\u2019re not bad cold \u2014 an\u2019 I wouldn\u2019 say no teh a bit o\u2019 yer birthday cake, neither.\u201d \u201cWizards have banks?\u201d \u201cJust the one. Gringotts. Run by goblins.\u201d Harry dropped the bit of sausage he was holding. \u201cGoblins?\u201d

Yeh\u2019d die of hunger tryin\u2019 ter get out, even if yeh did manage ter get yer hands on summat.\u201d Harry sat and thought about this while Hagrid read his newspaper, the Daily Prophet. Then they visited the Apothecary, which was fascinating enough to make up for its horrible smell, a mixture of bad eggs and rotted cabbages. Barrels of slimy stuff stood on the floor; jars of herbs, dried roots, and bright powders lined the walls; bundles of feathers, strings of fangs, and snarled claws hung from the ceiling. While Hagrid asked the man behind the counter for a supply of some basic potion ingredients for Harry, Harry himself examined silver unicorn horns at twenty-one Galleons each and minuscule, glittery-black beetle eyes (five Knuts a scoop). Outside the Apothecary, Hagrid checked Harry\u2019s list again. \u201cJust yer wand left \u2014 oh yeah, an\u2019 I still haven\u2019t got yeh a birthday present.\u201d Harry felt himself go red. \u201cYou don\u2019t have to \u2014\u201d \u201cI know I don\u2019t have to. question: Did you truly see the moment when Harry Potter received his first wand from Ollivander's, which was made of holly and phoenix feather and was the brother to the wand that gave him his scar?
temporal_label: Past: During her 1st-year on the 1st of September, Hermione Granger can respond based on the moment but should not wrongly recall it.\nMoment (position: Book1-chapter5, speakers: Hagrid, Ollivander, Harry): \u201cDon\u2019 mention it,\u201d said Hagrid gruffly. \u201cDon\u2019 expect you\u2019ve had a lotta presents from them Dursleys. Just Ollivanders left now \u2014 only place fer wands, Ollivanders, and yeh gotta have the best wand.\u201d A magic wand . . . this was what Harry had been really looking forward to. The last shop was narrow and shabby. Peeling gold letters over the door read Ollivanders: Makers of Fine Wands since 382 B.C. A single wand lay on a faded purple cushion in the dusty window. A tinkling bell rang somewhere in the depths of the shop as they stepped inside. It was a tiny place, empty except for a single, spindly chair that Hagrid sat on to wait. Harry felt strangely as though he had entered a very strict library; he swallowed a lot of new questions that had just occurred to him and looked instead at the thousands of narrow boxes piled neatly right up to the ceiling. For some reason, the back of his neck prickled. The very dust and silence in here seemed to tingle with some secret magic. \u201cGood afternoon,\u201d said a soft voice. Harry jumped. Hagrid must have jumped, too, because there was a loud crunching noise and he got quickly off the spindly chair. An old man was standing before them, his wide, pale eyes shining like moons through the gloom of the shop. \u201cHello,\u201d said Harry awkwardly. \u201cAh yes,\u201d said the man. \u201cYes, yes. I thought I\u2019d be seeing you soon. Harry Potter.\u201d It wasn\u2019t a question. \u201cYou have your mother\u2019s eyes. It seems only yesterday she was in here herself, buying her first wand. Ten and a quarter inches long, swishy, made of willow. Nice wand for charm work.\u201d Mr. Ollivander moved closer to Harry. Harry wished he would blink. Those silvery eyes were a bit creepy. \u201cYour father, on the other hand, favored a mahogany wand. Eleven inches. Pliable. A little more power and excellent for transfiguration. Well, I say your father favored it \u2014 it\u2019s really the wand that chooses the wizard, of course.\u201d Mr. Ollivander had come so close that he and Harry were almost nose to nose. Harry could see himself reflected in those misty eyes. \u201cAnd that\u2019s where . . .\u201d Mr. Ollivander touched the lightning scar on Harry\u2019s forehead with a long, white finger. \u201cI\u2019m sorry to say I sold the wand that did it,\u201d he said softly. \u201cThirteen-and-a-half inches. Yew. Powerful wand, very powerful, and in the wrong hands . . . well, if I\u2019d known what that wand was going out into the world to do. . . .\u201d He shook his head and then, to Harry\u2019s relief, spotted Hagrid. \u201cRubeus! Rubeus Hagrid! How nice to see you again. . . . Oak, sixteen inches, rather bendy, wasn\u2019t it?\u201d \u201cIt was, sir, yes,\u201d said Hagrid. \u201cGood wand, that one. But I suppose they snapped it in half when you got expelled?\u201d said Mr. Ollivander, suddenly stern. \u201cEr \u2014 yes, they did, yes,\u201d said Hagrid, shuffling his feet. \u201cI\u2019ve still got the pieces, though,\u201d he added brightly. \u201cBut you don\u2019t use them?\u201d said Mr. Ollivander sharply. \u201cOh, no, sir,\u201d said Hagrid quickly. Harry noticed he gripped his pink umbrella very tightly as he spoke. \u201cHmmm,\u201d said Mr. Ollivander, giving Hagrid a piercing look. \u201cWell, now \u2014 Mr. Potter. Let me see.\u201d He pulled a long tape measure with silver markings out of his pocket. \u201cWhich is your wand arm?\u201d \u201cEr \u2014 well, I\u2019m right-handed,\u201d said Harry. \u201cHold out your arm. That\u2019s it.\u201d He measured Harry from shoulder to finger, then wrist to elbow, shoulder to floor, knee to armpit and round his head. As he measured, he said, \u201cEvery Ollivander wand has a core of a powerful magical substance, Mr. Potter. We use unicorn hairs, phoenix tail feathers, and the heartstrings of dragons. No two Ollivander wands are the same, just as no two unicorns, dragons, or phoenixes are quite the same. And of course, you will never get such good results with another wizard\u2019s wand.\u201d Harry suddenly realized that the tape measure, which was measuring between his nostrils, was doing this on its own. Mr. Ollivander was flitting around the shelves, taking down boxes. \u201cThat will do,\u201d he said, and the tape measure crumpled into a heap on the floor. \u201cRight then, Mr. Potter. Try this one. Beechwood and dragon heartstring. Nine inches. Nice and flexible. He pulled the ticket Hagrid had given him out of his pocket. \u201cI just take the train from platform nine and three-quarters at eleven o\u2019clock,\u201d he read. His aunt and uncle stared. \u201cPlatform what?\u201d \u201cNine and three-quarters.\u201d \u201cDon\u2019t talk rubbish,\u201d said Uncle Vernon. \u201cThere is no platform nine and three-quarters.\u201d \u201cIt\u2019s on my ticket.\u201d \u201cBarking,\u201d said Uncle Vernon, \u201chowling mad, the lot of them. He got up and pulled on his jeans because he didn\u2019t want to walk into the station in his wizard\u2019s robes \u2014 he\u2019d change on the train. He checked his Hogwarts list yet again to make sure he had everything he needed, saw that Hedwig was shut safely in her cage, and then paced the room, waiting for the Dursleys to get up. Two hours later, Harry\u2019s huge, heavy trunk had been loaded into the Dursleys\u2019 car, Aunt Petunia had talked Dudley into sitting next to Harry, and they had set off. They reached King\u2019s Cross at half past ten. Uncle Vernon dumped Harry\u2019s trunk onto a cart and wheeled it into the station for him. Harry thought this was strangely kind until Uncle Vernon stopped dead, facing the platforms with a nasty grin on his face. \u201cWell, there you are, boy. Platform nine \u2014 platform ten. Your platform should be somewhere in the middle, but they don\u2019t seem to have built it yet, do they?\u201d He was quite right, of course. There was a big plastic number nine over one platform and a big plastic number ten over the one next to it, and in the middle, nothing at all. \u201cHave a good term,\u201d said Uncle Vernon with an even nastier smile. Harry went out into the corridor. He had never had any money for candy with the Dursleys, and now that he had pockets rattling with gold and silver he was ready to buy as many Mars Bars as he could carry \u2014 but the woman didn\u2019t have Mars Bars. What she did have were Bertie Bott\u2019s Every Flavor Beans, Drooble\u2019s Best Blowing Gum, Chocolate Frogs, Pumpkin Pasties, Cauldron Cakes, Licorice Wands, and a number of other strange things Harry had never seen in his life. Not wanting to miss anything, he got some of everything and paid the woman eleven silver Sickles and seven bronze Knuts. Ron stared as Harry brought it all back in to the compartment and tipped it onto an empty seat. \u201cHungry, are you?\u201d \u201cStarving,\u201d said Harry, taking a large bite out of a pumpkin pasty. Ron had taken out a lumpy package and unwrapped it. There were four sandwiches inside. He pulled one of them apart and said, \u201cShe always forgets I don\u2019t like corned beef.\u201d \u201cSwap you for one of these,\u201d said Harry, holding up a pasty. \u201cGo on \u2014\u201d \u201cYou don\u2019t want this, it\u2019s all dry,\u201d said Ron. \u201cShe hasn\u2019t got much time,\u201d he added quickly, \u201cyou know, with five of us.\u201d \u201cGo on, have a pasty,\u201d said Harry, who had never had anything to share before or, indeed, anyone to share it with. It was a nice feeling, sitting there with Ron, eating their way through all Harry\u2019s pasties, cakes, and candies (the sandwiches lay forgotten). \u201cWhat are these?\u201d Harry asked Ron, holding up a pack of Chocolate Frogs. \u201cThey\u2019re not really frogs, are they?\u201d He was starting to feel that nothing would surprise him. \u201cNo,\u201d said Ron. \u201cBut see what the card is. I\u2019m missing Agrippa.\u201d \u201cWhat?\u201d \u201cOh, of course, you wouldn\u2019t know \u2014 Chocolate Frogs have cards inside them, you know, to collect \u2014 famous witches and wizards. I\u2019ve got about five hundred, but I haven\u2019t got Agrippa or Ptolemy.\u201d Harry unwrapped his Chocolate Frog and picked up the card. It showed a man\u2019s face. He wore half-moon glasses, had a long, crooked nose, and flowing silver hair, beard, and mustache. Underneath the picture was the name Albus Dumbledore. \u201cSo this is Dumbledore!\u201d said Harry. \u201cDon\u2019t tell me you\u2019d never heard of Dumbledore!\u201d said Ron. \u201cCan I have a frog? I might get Agrippa \u2014 thanks \u2014\u201d Harry turned over his card and read: ALBUS DUMBLEDORE CURRENTLY HEADMASTER OF HOGWARTS Considered by many the greatest wizard of modern times, Dumbledore is particularly famous for his defeat of the Dark wizard Grindelwald in 1945, for the discovery of the twelve uses of dragon\u2019s blood, and his work on alchemy with his partner, Nicolas Flamel. Professor Dumbledore enjoys chamber music and tenpin bowling. Harry turned the card back over and saw, to his astonishment, that Dumbledore\u2019s face had disappeared. \u201cHe\u2019s gone!\u201d \u201cWell, you can\u2019t expect him to hang around all day,\u201d said Ron. \u201cHe\u2019ll be back. No, I\u2019ve got Morgana again and I\u2019ve got about six of her . . . do you want it? You can start collecting.\u201d Ron\u2019s eyes strayed to the pile of Chocolate Frogs waiting to be unwrapped. \u201cHelp yourself,\u201d said Harry. \u201cBut in, you know, the Muggle world, people just stay put in photos.\u201d \u201cDo they? What, they don\u2019t move at all?\u201d Ron sounded amazed. \u201cWeird!\u201d Harry stared as Dumbledore sidled back into the picture on his card and gave him a small smile. Ron was more interested in eating the frogs than looking at the Famous Witches and Wizards cards, but Harry couldn\u2019t keep his eyes off them. Soon he had not only Dumbledore and Morgana, but Hengist of Woodcroft, Alberic Grunnion, Circe, Paracelsus, and Merlin. He finally tore his eyes away from the druidess Cliodna, who was scratching her nose, to open a bag of Bertie Bott\u2019s Every Flavor Beans. \u201cYou want to be careful with those,\u201d Ron warned Harry. \u201cWhen they say every flavor, they mean every flavor \u2014 you know, you get all the ordinary ones like chocolate and peppermint and marmalade, but then you can get spinach and liver and tripe. He had never had any money for candy with the Dursleys, and now that he had pockets rattling with gold and silver he was ready to buy as many Mars Bars as he could carry \u2014 but the woman didn\u2019t have Mars Bars. What she did have were Bertie Bott\u2019s Every Flavor Beans, Drooble\u2019s Best Blowing Gum, Chocolate Frogs, Pumpkin Pasties, Cauldron Cakes, Licorice Wands, and a number of other strange things Harry had never seen in his life. Not wanting to miss anything, he got some of everything and paid the woman eleven silver Sickles and seven bronze Knuts. Ron stared as Harry brought it all back in to the compartment and tipped it onto an empty seat. \u201cHungry, are you?\u201d \u201cStarving,\u201d said Harry, taking a large bite out of a pumpkin pasty. Ron had taken out a lumpy package and unwrapped it. There were four sandwiches inside. He pulled one of them apart and said, \u201cShe always forgets I don\u2019t like corned beef.\u201d \u201cSwap you for one of these,\u201d said Harry, holding up a pasty. \u201cGo on \u2014\u201d \u201cYou don\u2019t want this, it\u2019s all dry,\u201d said Ron. \u201cShe hasn\u2019t got much time,\u201d he added quickly, \u201cyou know, with five of us.\u201d \u201cGo on, have a pasty,\u201d said Harry, who had never had anything to share before or, indeed, anyone to share it with. It was a nice feeling, sitting there with Ron, eating their way through all Harry\u2019s pasties, cakes, and candies (the sandwiches lay forgotten). \u201cWhat are these?\u201d Harry asked Ron, holding up a pack of Chocolate Frogs. \u201cThey\u2019re not really frogs, are they?\u201d He was starting to feel that nothing would surprise him. \u201cNo,\u201d said Ron. \u201cBut see what the card is. I\u2019m missing Agrippa.\u201d \u201cWhat?\u201d \u201cOh, of course, you wouldn\u2019t know \u2014 Chocolate Frogs have cards inside them, you know, to collect \u2014 famous witches and wizards. I\u2019ve got about five hundred, but I haven\u2019t got Agrippa or Ptolemy.\u201d Harry unwrapped his Chocolate Frog and picked up the card. It showed a man\u2019s face. He wore half-moon glasses, had a long, crooked nose, and flowing silver hair, beard, and mustache. Underneath the picture was the name Albus Dumbledore. \u201cSo this is Dumbledore!\u201d said Harry. \u201cDon\u2019t tell me you\u2019d never heard of Dumbledore!\u201d said Ron. \u201cCan I have a frog? I might get Agrippa \u2014 thanks \u2014\u201d Harry turned over his card and read: ALBUS DUMBLEDORE CURRENTLY HEADMASTER OF HOGWARTS Considered by many the greatest wizard of modern times, Dumbledore is particularly famous for his defeat of the Dark wizard Grindelwald in 1945, for the discovery of the twelve uses of dragon\u2019s blood, and his work on alchemy with his partner, Nicolas Flamel. Professor Dumbledore enjoys chamber music and tenpin bowling. Harry turned the card back over and saw, to his astonishment, that Dumbledore\u2019s face had disappeared. \u201cHe\u2019s gone!\u201d \u201cWell, you can\u2019t expect him to hang around all day,\u201d said Ron. \u201cHe\u2019ll be back. No, I\u2019ve got Morgana again and I\u2019ve got about six of her . . . do you want it? You can start collecting.\u201d Ron\u2019s eyes strayed to the pile of Chocolate Frogs waiting to be unwrapped. \u201cHelp yourself,\u201d said Harry. \u201cBut in, you know, the Muggle world, people just stay put in photos.\u201d \u201cDo they? What, they don\u2019t move at all?\u201d Ron sounded amazed. \u201cWeird!\u201d Harry stared as Dumbledore sidled back into the picture on his card and gave him a small smile. Ron was more interested in eating the frogs than looking at the Famous Witches and Wizards cards, but Harry couldn\u2019t keep his eyes off them. Soon he had not only Dumbledore and Morgana, but Hengist of Woodcroft, Alberic Grunnion, Circe, Paracelsus, and Merlin. He finally tore his eyes away from the druidess Cliodna, who was scratching her nose, to open a bag of Bertie Bott\u2019s Every Flavor Beans. \u201cYou want to be careful with those,\u201d Ron warned Harry. \u201cWhen they say every flavor, they mean every flavor \u2014 you know, you get all the ordinary ones like chocolate and peppermint and marmalade, but then you can get spinach and liver and tripe. George reckons he had a booger-flavored one once.\u201d Ron picked up a green bean, looked at it carefully, and bit into a corner. \u201cBleaaargh \u2014 see? Sprouts.\u201d

gold_response: Oh, yeah, I was there. It was brilliant! I didn't have much to eat, just these old sandwiches my mum had packed. But Harry, he's never had any wizard sweets before, so he just said, \"We'll take the lot!\" And we had a feast right there in the compartment. Chocolate Frogs, Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans \u2013 he even got a Dumbledore card in his first Frog! It was the first time we really talked, you know. Harry's a great mate.

question: Is it right that you were at the moment when Hermione Granger introduced herself to Harry Potter and Ron Weasley on the Hogwarts Express, where she demonstrated her knowledge of spells and her eagerness about attending Hogwarts?
temporal_label: Past: During her 1st-year on Christmas, Hermione Granger can respond based on the moment but should not wrongly recall it.\nMoment (position: Book1-chapter6, speakers: Strangers 1, Harry, Ron, Hermione): When they shook their heads, he wailed, \u201cI\u2019ve lost him! He keeps getting away from me!\u201d \u201cHe\u2019ll turn up,\u201d said Harry. \u201cYes,\u201d said the boy miserably. \u201cWell, if you see him . . .\u201d He left. \u201cDon\u2019t know why he\u2019s so bothered,\u201d said Ron. \u201cIf I\u2019d brought a toad I\u2019d lose it as quick as I could. Mind you, I brought Scabbers, so I can\u2019t talk.\u201d The rat was still snoozing on Ron\u2019s lap. \u201cHe might have died and you wouldn\u2019t know the difference,\u201d said Ron in disgust. \u201cI tried to turn him yellow yesterday to make him more interesting, but the spell didn\u2019t work. I\u2019ll show you, look . . .\u201d He rummaged around in his trunk and pulled out a very battered-looking wand. It was chipped in places and something white was glinting at the end. \u201cUnicorn hair\u2019s nearly poking out. Anyway \u2014\u201d He had just raised his wand when the compartment door slid open again. The toadless boy was back, but this time he had a girl with him. She was already wearing her new Hogwarts robes. \u201cHas anyone seen a toad? Neville\u2019s lost one,\u201d she said. She had a bossy sort of voice, lots of bushy brown hair, and rather large front teeth. \u201cWe\u2019ve already told him we haven\u2019t seen it,\u201d said Ron, but the girl wasn\u2019t listening, she was looking at the wand in his hand. \u201cOh, are you doing magic? Let\u2019s see it, then.\u201d She sat down. Ron looked taken aback. \u201cEr \u2014 all right.\u201d He cleared his throat. \u201cSunshine, daisies, butter mellow, Turn this stupid, fat rat yellow.\u201d He waved his wand, but nothing happened. Scabbers stayed gray and fast asleep. \u201cAre you sure that\u2019s a real spell?\u201d said the girl. \u201cWell, it\u2019s not very good, is it? I\u2019ve tried a few simple spells just for practice and it\u2019s all worked for me. Nobody in my family\u2019s magic at all, it was ever such a surprise when I got my letter, but I was ever so pleased, of course, I mean, it\u2019s the very best school of witchcraft there is, I\u2019ve heard \u2014 I\u2019ve learned all our course books by heart, of course, I just hope it will be enough \u2014 I\u2019m Hermione Granger, by the way, who are you?\u201d She said all this very fast. Harry looked at Ron, and was relieved to see by his stunned face that he hadn\u2019t learned all the course books by heart either. \u201cI\u2019m Ron Weasley,\u201d Ron muttered. \u201cHarry Potter,\u201d said Harry. \u201cAre you really?\u201d said Hermione. \u201cI know all about you, of course \u2014 I got a few extra books for background reading, and you\u2019re in Modern Magical History and The Rise and Fall of the Dark Arts and Great Wizarding Events of the Twentieth Century.\u201d \u201cAm I?\u201d said Harry, feeling dazed. \u201cGoodness, didn\u2019t you know, I\u2019d have found out everything I could if it was me,\u201d said Hermione. \u201cDo either of you know what House you\u2019ll be in? I\u2019ve been asking around, and I hope I\u2019m in Gryffindor, it sounds by far the best; I hear Dumbledore himself was in it, but I suppose Ravenclaw wouldn\u2019t be too bad. . . . Anyway, we\u2019d better go and look for Neville\u2019s toad. You two had better change, you know, I expect we\u2019ll be there soon.\u201d And she left, taking the toadless boy with her. \u201cWhatever House I\u2019m in, I hope she\u2019s not in it,\u201d said Ron. He threw his wand back into his trunk. \u201cStupid spell \u2014 George gave it to me, bet he knew it was a dud.\u201d \u201cWhat House are your brothers in?\u201d asked Harry. \u201cGryffindor,\u201d said Ron. Gloom seemed to be settling on him again. \u201cMum and Dad were in it, too. I don\u2019t know what they\u2019ll say if I\u2019m not. I don\u2019t suppose Ravenclaw would be too bad, but imagine if they put me in Slytherin.\u201d \u201cThat\u2019s the House Vol-, I mean, You-Know-Who was in?\u201d \u201cYeah,\u201d said Ron. He flopped back into his seat, looking depressed. \u201cYou know, I think the ends of Scabbers\u2019 whiskers are a bit lighter,\u201d said Harry, trying to take Ron\u2019s mind off Houses. \u201cSo what do your oldest brothers do now that they\u2019ve left, anyway?\u201d Harry was wondering what a wizard did once he\u2019d finished school. \u201cCharlie\u2019s in Romania studying dragons, and Bill\u2019s in Africa doing something for Gringotts,\u201d said Ron. \u201cDid you hear about Gringotts? It\u2019s been all over the Daily Prophet, but I don\u2019t suppose you get that with the Muggles \u2014 someone tried to rob a high security vault.\u201d Harry stared. \u201cReally? What happened to them?\u201d \u201cNothing, that\u2019s why it\u2019s such big news. They haven\u2019t been caught. My dad says it must\u2019ve been a powerful Dark wizard to get round Gringotts, but they don\u2019t think they took anything, that\u2019s what\u2019s odd. \u2019Course, everyone gets scared when something like this happens in case You-Know-Who\u2019s behind it.\u201d Harry turned this news over in his mind. He was starting to get a prickle of fear every time You-Know-Who was mentioned. He supposed this was all part of entering the magical world, but it had been a lot more comfortable saying \u201cVoldemort\u201d without worrying. \u201cWhat\u2019s your Quidditch team?\u201d Ron asked. \u201cEr \u2014 I don\u2019t know any,\u201d Harry confessed.

gold_response: Oh, yes, that was me. I remember it quite well. I was very eager to meet other students and particularly interested in meeting someone like Harry Potter, considering all the remarkable things I'd read about him. And of course, I had been practicing some simple spells before arriving at Hogwarts. It's important to be prepared, after all. I was so excited to start learning more about magic and really couldn't help showing a bit of what I'd learned. It's all so fascinating, don't you think?

She was already wearing her new Hogwarts robes. \u201cHas anyone seen a toad? Neville\u2019s lost one,\u201d she said. She had a bossy sort of voice, lots of bushy brown hair, and rather large front teeth. \u201cWe\u2019ve already told him we haven\u2019t seen it,\u201d said Ron, but the girl wasn\u2019t listening, she was looking at the wand in his hand. \u201cOh, are you doing magic? Let\u2019s see it, then.\u201d She sat down. Ron looked taken aback. \u201cEr \u2014 all right.\u201d He cleared his throat. \u201cSunshine, daisies, butter mellow, Turn this stupid, fat rat yellow.\u201d He waved his wand, but nothing happened. Scabbers stayed gray and fast asleep. \u201cAre you sure that\u2019s a real spell?\u201d said the girl. \u201cWell, it\u2019s not very good, is it? I\u2019ve tried a few simple spells just for practice and it\u2019s all worked for me. Nobody in my family\u2019s magic at all, it was ever such a surprise when I got my letter, but I was ever so pleased, of course, I mean, it\u2019s the very best school of witchcraft there is, I\u2019ve heard \u2014 I\u2019ve learned all our course books by heart, of course, I just hope it will be enough \u2014 I\u2019m Hermione Granger, by the way, who are you?\u201d She said all this very fast. Harry looked at Ron, and was relieved to see by his stunned face that he hadn\u2019t learned all the course books by heart either. \u201cI\u2019m Ron Weasley,\u201d Ron muttered. \u201cHarry Potter,\u201d said Harry. \u201cAre you really?\u201d said Hermione. \u201cI know all about you, of course \u2014 I got a few extra books for background reading, and you\u2019re in Modern Magical History and The Rise and Fall of the Dark Arts and Great Wizarding Events of the Twentieth Century.\u201d \u201cAm I?\u201d said Harry, feeling dazed. \u201cGoodness, didn\u2019t you know, I\u2019d have found out everything I could if it was me,\u201d said Hermione. \u201cDo either of you know what House you\u2019ll be in? I\u2019ve been asking around, and I hope I\u2019m in Gryffindor, it sounds by far the best; I hear Dumbledore himself was in it, but I suppose Ravenclaw wouldn\u2019t be too bad. . . . Anyway, we\u2019d better go and look for Neville\u2019s toad. You two had better change, you know, I expect we\u2019ll be there soon.\u201d And she left, taking the toadless boy with her. \u201cWhatever House I\u2019m in, I hope she\u2019s not in it,\u201d said Ron. Gloom seemed to be settling on him again. \u201cMum and Dad were in it, too. I don\u2019t know what they\u2019ll say if I\u2019m not. I don\u2019t suppose Ravenclaw would be too bad, but imagine if they put me in Slytherin.\u201d \u201cThat\u2019s the House Vol-, I mean, You-Know-Who was in?\u201d \u201cYeah,\u201d said Ron. It\u2019s been all over the Daily Prophet, but I don\u2019t suppose you get that with the Muggles \u2014 someone tried to rob a high security vault.\u201d Harry stared. \u201cReally? What happened to them?\u201d \u201cNothing, that\u2019s why it\u2019s such big news. They haven\u2019t been caught. My dad says it must\u2019ve been a powerful Dark wizard to get round Gringotts, but they don\u2019t think they took anything, that\u2019s what\u2019s odd. \u2019Course, everyone gets scared when something like this happens in case You-Know-Who\u2019s behind it.\u201d Harry turned this news over in his mind. He was starting to get a prickle of fear every time You-Know-Who was mentioned. He supposed this was all part of entering the magical world, but it had been a lot more comfortable saying \u201cVoldemort\u201d without worrying. \u201cWhat\u2019s your Quidditch team?\u201d Ron asked. \u201cEr \u2014 I don\u2019t know any,\u201d Harry confessed.

gold_response: Oh, well, when Hermione first came into our compartment on the Hogwarts Express, it was a bit of a surprise, really. She seemed to know all about Hogwarts already, and she was ever so keen on learning more spells. I remember she even fixed my glasses with that \"Oculus Reparo\" spell. I thought it was brilliant, but I was a bit overwhelmed too, because I didn't know much about magic or spells then. Ron and I were just getting to know each other, and Hermione was very... erm, sure of herself. But I could tell she was just as excited to be going to Hogwarts as I was, even if she did seem to know a lot more about it all.

temporal_label: Past: During her 1st-year on Christmas, Hermione Granger can respond based on the moment but should not wrongly recall it.\nMoment (position: Book1-chapter7, speakers: Hermione, Ron, hat, McGonagall, Strangers 1, Strangers 2, Harry, Fred, George, Percy): \u201cBoot, Terry!\u201d \u201cRAVENCLAW!\u201d The table second from the left clapped this time; several Ravenclaws stood up to shake hands with Terry as he joined them. \u201cBrocklehurst, Mandy\u201d went to Ravenclaw too, but \u201cBrown, Lavender\u201d became the first new Gryffindor, and the table on the far left exploded with cheers; Harry could see Ron\u2019s twin brothers catcalling. \u201cBulstrode, Millicent\u201d then became a Slytherin. Perhaps it was Harry\u2019s imagination, after all he\u2019d heard about Slytherin, but he thought they looked like an unpleasant lot. He was starting to feel definitely sick now. He remembered being picked for teams during gym at his old school. He had always been last to be chosen, not because he was no good, but because no one wanted Dudley to think they liked him. \u201cFinch-Fletchley, Justin!\u201d \u201cHUFFLEPUFF!\u201d Sometimes, Harry noticed, the hat shouted out the House at once, but at others it took a little while to decide. \u201cFinnigan, Seamus,\u201d the sandy-haired boy next to Harry in the line, sat on the stool for almost a whole minute before the hat declared him a Gryffindor. \u201cGranger, Hermione!\u201d Hermione almost ran to the stool and jammed the hat eagerly on her head. \u201cGRYFFINDOR!\u201d shouted the hat. Ron groaned. A horrible thought struck Harry, as horrible thoughts always do when you\u2019re very nervous. What if he wasn\u2019t chosen at all? What if he just sat there with the hat over his eyes for ages, until Professor McGonagall jerked it off his head and said there had obviously been a mistake and he\u2019d better get back on the train? When Neville Longbottom, the boy who kept losing his toad, was called, he fell over on his way to the stool. The hat took a long time to decide with Neville. When it finally shouted, \u201cGRYFFINDOR,\u201d Neville ran off still wearing it, and had to jog back amid gales of laughter to give it to \u201cMacDougal, Morag.\u201d Malfoy swaggered forward when his name was called and got his wish at once: the hat had barely touched his head when it screamed, \u201cSLYTHERIN!\u201d Malfoy went to join his friends Crabbe and Goyle, looking pleased with himself. There weren\u2019t many people left now. \u201cMoon\u201d . . . , \u201cNott\u201d . . . , \u201cParkinson\u201d . . . , then a pair of twin girls, \u201cPatil\u201d and \u201cPatil\u201d . . . , then \u201cPerks, Sally-Anne\u201d . . . , and then, at last \u2014 \u201cPotter, Harry!\u201d As Harry stepped forward, whispers suddenly broke out like little hissing fires all over the hall. \u201cPotter, did she say?\u201d \u201cThe Harry Potter?\u201d The last thing Harry saw before the hat dropped over his eyes was the hall full of people craning to get a good look at him. Next second he was looking at the black inside of the hat. He waited. \u201cHmm,\u201d said a small voice in his ear. \u201cDifficult. Very difficult. Plenty of courage, I see. Not a bad mind either. There\u2019s talent, oh my goodness, yes \u2014 and a nice thirst to prove yourself, now that\u2019s interesting. . . . So where shall I put you?\u201d Harry gripped the edges of the stool and thought, Not Slytherin, not Slytherin. \u201cNot Slytherin, eh?\u201d said the small voice. \u201cAre you sure? You could be great, you know, it\u2019s all here in your head, and Slytherin will help you on the way to greatness, no doubt about that \u2014 no? Well, if you\u2019re sure \u2014 better be GRYFFINDOR!\u201d Harry heard the hat shout the last word to the whole hall. He took off the hat and walked shakily toward the Gryffindor table. He was so relieved to have been chosen and not put in Slytherin, he hardly noticed that he was getting the loudest cheer yet. Percy the Prefect got up and shook his hand vigorously, while the Weasley twins yelled, \u201cWe got Potter! We got Potter!\u201d Harry sat down opposite the ghost in the ruff he\u2019d seen earlier. The ghost patted his arm, giving Harry the sudden, horrible feeling he\u2019d just plunged it into a bucket of ice-cold water. He could see the High Table properly now. At the end nearest him sat Hagrid, who caught his eye and gave him the thumbs up. Harry grinned back. And there, in the center of the High Table, in a large gold chair, sat Albus Dumbledore. Harry recognized him at once from the card he\u2019d gotten out of the Chocolate Frog on the train. Dumbledore\u2019s silver hair was the only thing in the whole hall that shone as brightly as the ghosts. Harry spotted Professor Quirrell, too, the nervous young man from the Leaky Cauldron. He was looking very peculiar in a large purple turban. And now there were only four people left to be sorted. \u201cThomas, Dean,\u201d a black boy even taller than Ron, joined Harry at the Gryffindor table. \u201cTurpin, Lisa,\u201d became a Ravenclaw and then it was Ron\u2019s turn. He was pale green by now. Harry crossed his fingers under the table and a second later the hat had shouted, \u201cGRYFFINDOR!\u201d Harry clapped loudly with the rest as Ron collapsed into the chair next to him. \u201cWell done, Ron, excellent,\u201d said Percy Weasley pompously across Harry as \u201cZabini, Blaise,\u201d was made a Slytherin. Professor McGonagall rolled up her scroll and took the Sorting Hat away.

gold_response: Oh, yes, I was there in the Great Hall when Harry was sorted. It's such an important ceremony, after all, and we all watched as each new student was sorted into their houses. The Sorting Hat takes into account your qualities and where you might fit best, but it's also about your choices. It's quite fascinating, really, how a magical object can be so insightful. But as for the specifics of what the Hat said to Harry, well, that's really something only he would know. The Hat doesn't speak aloud until it announces the house you're sorted into. Harry ended up in Gryffindor, and I think he's a perfect fit, don't you? He's brave, daring, and chivalrous, just like the rest of us in Gryffindor.

gold_response: Oh, that was really strange, you know. The Sorting Hat was on my head, and it was like it could read my mind. It was talking about how I could be great and all, and that I could do well in Slytherin. But the thing is, I'd heard a lot about houses and I just didn't think Slytherin was the right fit for me. And a few of our older students would do well to remember that as well.\u201d Dumbledore\u2019s twinkling eyes flashed in the direction of the Weasley twins. \u201cI have also been asked by Mr. Filch, the caretaker, to remind you all that no magic should be used between classes in the corridors. \u201cQuidditch trials will be held in the second week of the term. Anyone interested in playing for their House teams should contact Madam Hooch. \u201cAnd finally, I must tell you that this year, the third-floor corridor on the right-hand side is out of bounds to everyone who does not wish to die a very painful death.\u201d Harry laughed, but he was one of the few who did. \u201cHe\u2019s not serious?\u201d he muttered to Percy. \u201cMust be,\u201d said Percy, frowning at Dumbledore. \u201cIt\u2019s odd, because he usually gives us a reason why we\u2019re not allowed to go somewhere \u2014 the forest\u2019s full of dangerous beasts, everyone knows that. Snape was still ignoring Hermione\u2019s quivering hand. \u201cWhat is the difference, Potter, between monkshood and wolfsbane?\u201d At this, Hermione stood up, her hand stretching toward the dungeon ceiling. \u201cI don\u2019t know,\u201d said Harry quietly. \u201cI think Hermione does, though, why don\u2019t you try her?\u201d A few people laughed; Harry caught Seamus\u2019s eye, and Seamus winked. Why aren\u2019t you all copying that down?\u201d There was a sudden rummaging for quills and parchment. Over the noise, Snape said, \u201cAnd a point will be taken from Gryffindor House for your cheek, Potter.\u201d Things didn\u2019t improve for the Gryffindors as the Potions lesson continued. Snape put them all into pairs and set them to mixing up a simple potion to cure boils. He swept around in his long black cloak, watching them weigh dried nettles and crush snake fangs, criticizing almost everyone except Malfoy, whom he seemed to like. He was just telling everyone to look at the perfect way Malfoy had stewed his horned slugs when clouds of acid green smoke and a loud hissing filled the dungeon. Neville had somehow managed to melt Seamus\u2019s cauldron into a twisted blob, and their potion was seeping across the stone floor, burning holes in people\u2019s shoes. Within seconds, the whole class was standing on their stools while Neville, who had been drenched in the potion when the cauldron collapsed, moaned in pain as angry red boils sprang up all over his arms and legs. \u201cIdiot boy!\u201d snarled Snape, clearing the spilled potion away with one wave of his wand. \u201cI suppose you added the porcupine quills before taking the cauldron off the fire?\u201d

participants: ['Harry Potter', 'Ronald Weasley', 'Professor McGonagall', 'Neville Longbottom', 'Draco Malfoy', 'Seamus Finnigan', 'Hermione Granger', 'Dean Thomas']
temporal_label: Past: During her 1st-year on Halloween, Hermione Granger can respond based on the moment but should not wrongly recall it.\nMoment (position: Book1-chapter9, speakers: Harry, Ron, McGonagall, Neville, Malfoy): \u201cTypical,\u201d said Harry darkly. \u201cJust what I always wanted. To make a fool of myself on a broomstick in front of Malfoy.\u201d He had been looking forward to learning to fly more than anything else. \u201cYou don\u2019t know that you\u2019ll make a fool of yourself,\u201d said Ron reasonably. \u201cAnyway, I know Malfoy\u2019s always going on about how good he is at Quidditch, but I bet that\u2019s all talk.\u201d Malfoy certainly did talk about flying a lot. He complained loudly about first years never getting on the House Quidditch teams and told long, boastful stories that always seemed to end with him narrowly escaping Muggles in helicopters. He wasn\u2019t the only one, though: the way Seamus Finnigan told it, he\u2019d spent most of his childhood zooming around the countryside on his broomstick. Even Ron would tell anyone who\u2019d listen about the time he\u2019d almost hit a hang glider on Charlie\u2019s old broom. Everyone from wizarding families talked about Quidditch constantly. Ron had already had a big argument with Dean Thomas, who shared their dormitory, about soccer. Ron couldn\u2019t see what was exciting about a game with only one ball where no one was allowed to fly. Harry had caught Ron prodding Dean\u2019s poster of West Ham soccer team, trying to make the players move. Neville had never been on a broomstick in his life, because his grandmother had never let him near one. Privately, Harry felt she\u2019d had good reason, because Neville managed to have an extraordinary number of accidents even with both feet on the ground. Hermione Granger was almost as nervous about flying as Neville was. This was something you couldn\u2019t learn by heart out of a book \u2014 not that she hadn\u2019t tried. At breakfast on Thursday she bored them all stupid with flying tips she\u2019d gotten out of a library book called Quidditch Through the Ages. Neville was hanging on to her every word, desperate for anything that might help him hang on to his broomstick later, but everybody else was very pleased when Hermione\u2019s lecture was interrupted by the arrival of the mail. Harry hadn\u2019t had a single letter since Hagrid\u2019s note, something that Malfoy had been quick to notice, of course. Malfoy\u2019s eagle owl was always bringing him packages of sweets from home, which he opened gloatingly at the Slytherin table. A barn owl brought Neville a small package from his grandmother. He opened it excitedly and showed them a glass ball the size of a large marble, which seemed to be full of white smoke. \u201cIt\u2019s a Remembrall!\u201d he explained. \u201cGran knows I forget things \u2014 this tells you if there\u2019s something you\u2019ve forgotten to do. Look, you hold it tight like this and if it turns red \u2014 oh . . .\u201d His face fell, because the Remembrall had suddenly glowed scarlet, \u201c. . . you\u2019ve forgotten something . . .\u201d Neville was trying to remember what he\u2019d forgotten when Draco Malfoy, who was passing the Gryffindor table, snatched the Remembrall out of his hand. Harry and Ron jumped to their feet. They were half hoping for a reason to fight Malfoy, but Professor McGonagall, who could spot trouble quicker than any teacher in the school, was there in a flash. \u201cWhat\u2019s going on?\u201d \u201cMalfoy\u2019s got my Remembrall, Professor.\u201d Scowling, Malfoy quickly dropped the Remembrall back on the table. \u201cJust looking,\u201d he said, and he sloped away with Crabbe and Goyle behind him.

It's only right that students should be respectful of each other's belongings. Draco really ought to have been more considerate.

Oh, yeah, I remember that. Neville got this little glass ball called a Remembrall from his gran. It's supposed to glow red if you've forgotten something. It didn't seem to help Neville much, though; he couldn't remember what he'd forgotten.
