question: Were you indeed present as Oliver Wood introduced Harry Potter to the rules and equipment of Quidditch, explaining the roles of the players and the functions of the different balls, including the Golden Snitch?
temporal_label: Past: At the end of the scene of Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone as a 1st-year student, Hermione Granger can respond based on the moment but should not wrongly recall it.\nMoment (position: Book1-chapter10, speakers: Wood, Harry): \u201cHey, Potter, come down!\u201d Oliver Wood had arrived. He was carrying a large wooden crate under his arm. Harry landed next to him. \u201cVery nice,\u201d said Wood, his eyes glinting. \u201cI see what McGonagall meant . . . you really are a natural. I\u2019m just going to teach you the rules this evening, then you\u2019ll be joining team practice three times a week.\u201d He opened the crate. Inside were four different-sized balls. \u201cRight,\u201d said Wood. \u201cNow, Quidditch is easy enough to understand, even if it\u2019s not too easy to play. There are seven players on each side. Three of them are called Chasers.\u201d \u201cThree Chasers,\u201d Harry repeated, as Wood took out a bright red ball about the size of a soccer ball. \u201cThis ball\u2019s called the Quaffle,\u201d said Wood. \u201cThe Chasers throw the Quaffle to each other and try and get it through one of the hoops to score a goal. Ten points every time the Quaffle goes through one of the hoops. Follow me?\u201d \u201cThe Chasers throw the Quaffle and put it through the hoops to score,\u201d Harry recited. \u201cSo \u2014 that\u2019s sort of like basketball on broomsticks with six hoops, isn\u2019t it?\u201d \u201cWhat\u2019s basketball?\u201d said Wood curiously. \u201cNever mind,\u201d said Harry quickly. \u201cNow, there\u2019s another player on each side who\u2019s called the Keeper \u2014 I\u2019m Keeper for Gryffindor. I have to fly around our hoops and stop the other team from scoring.\u201d \u201cThree Chasers, one Keeper,\u201d said Harry, who was determined to remember it all. \u201cAnd they play with the Quaffle. Okay, got that. So what are they for?\u201d He pointed at the three balls left inside the box. \u201cI\u2019ll show you now,\u201d said Wood. \u201cTake this.\u201d He handed Harry a small club, a bit like a short baseball bat. \u201cI\u2019m going to show you what the Bludgers do,\u201d Wood said. \u201cThese two are the Bludgers.\u201d He showed Harry two identical balls, jet black and slightly smaller than the red Quaffle. Harry noticed that they seemed to be straining to escape the straps holding them inside the box. \u201cStand back,\u201d Wood warned Harry. He bent down and freed one of the Bludgers. At once, the black ball rose high in the air and then pelted straight at Harry\u2019s face. Harry swung at it with the bat to stop it from breaking his nose, and sent it zigzagging away into the air \u2014 it zoomed around their heads and then shot at Wood, who dived on top of it and managed to pin it to the ground. \u201cSee?\u201d Wood panted, forcing the struggling Bludger back into the crate and strapping it down safely. \u201cThe Bludgers rocket around, trying to knock players off their brooms. That\u2019s why you have two Beaters on each team \u2014 the Weasley twins are ours \u2014 it\u2019s their job to protect their side from the Bludgers and try and knock them toward the other team. So \u2014 think you\u2019ve got all that?\u201d \u201cThree Chasers try and score with the Quaffle; the Keeper guards the goalposts; the Beaters keep the Bludgers away from their team,\u201d Harry reeled off. \u201cVery good,\u201d said Wood. \u201cEr \u2014 have the Bludgers ever killed anyone?\u201d Harry asked, hoping he sounded offhand. \u201cNever at Hogwarts. We\u2019ve had a couple of broken jaws but nothing worse than that. Now, the last member of the team is the Seeker. That\u2019s you. And you don\u2019t have to worry about the Quaffle or the Bludgers \u2014\u201d \u201c\u2014 unless they crack my head open.\u201d \u201cDon\u2019t worry, the Weasleys are more than a match for the Bludgers \u2014 I mean, they\u2019re like a pair of human Bludgers themselves.\u201d Wood reached into the crate and took out the fourth and last ball. Compared with the Quaffle and the Bludgers, it was tiny, about the size of a large walnut. It was bright gold and had little fluttering silver wings. \u201cThis,\u201d said Wood, \u201cis the Golden Snitch, and it\u2019s the most important ball of the lot. It\u2019s very hard to catch because it\u2019s so fast and difficult to see. It\u2019s the Seeker\u2019s job to catch it. You\u2019ve got to weave in and out of the Chasers, Beaters, Bludgers, and Quaffle to get it before the other team\u2019s Seeker, because whichever Seeker catches the Snitch wins his team an extra hundred and fifty points, so they nearly always win. That\u2019s why Seekers get fouled so much. A game of Quidditch only ends when the Snitch is caught, so it can go on for ages \u2014 I think the record is three months, they had to keep bringing on substitutes so the players could get some sleep. \u201cWell, that\u2019s it \u2014 any questions?\u201d
